reading: North Korea invaded 25 Jun; first trading day fell -5.4% -- the sharpest since 1946. The fear was not Korea but that this was the OPENING MOVE of a general US-USSR war.
The selloff ran ~three weeks to a -12.9% trough. A war scare that DID move Wall Street -- because it read as potentially general.
MacArthur's Inchon landing; the war looked contained/winnable. The general-war premium evaporated -- fully recovered past the pre-invasion level.
China's massive intervention (~26-28 Nov) routed UN forces; Truman's 30 Nov atomic-bomb remark spooked markets/allies. General-war fear RETURNED and the market broke again -6.5%.
As the war revealed itself as limited (no atomic use; stalemate; MacArthur relieved Apr 1951), the premium faded again and the market made new highs above pre-invasion.
